sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: permits, tests and license classes
Confusable pairs a first-time applicant mixes up, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in the trailing lines.

FACT_ID: sec01-R01 | anchor: A01
A learner permit and a license differ in supervision: the permit holder may drive only with a person licensed for that vehicle seated alongside, while a licensed driver may drive alone. [A01]
Why it matters: group permits; prereq none; difficulty low; confusable with provisional licensing rules in the graduated licensing section.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-R02 | anchor: A01
The learner permit tests are vision, signs and motor vehicle law knowledge, while an original license can also require the on-road driving skill test. [A01]
Why it matters: group testing; confusable permit tests versus license tests.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-R03 | anchor: A02
The signs test and the knowledge test are not the same test: the signs test asks you to identify signs by color and shape and give their meaning, while the knowledge test covers traffic laws and safe driving practices. [A02]
Why it matters: group testing; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R04 | anchor: A02
The road test is the final step for a first license, but it is not required for a learner permit, and it may or may not be required at renewal. [A02]
Why it matters: group testing; confusable first license versus renewal versus permit.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R05 | anchor: A02
A corrective-lens restriction is not a suggestion: driving without the required lenses is treated like driving unlicensed, not like a minor equipment fault. [A02]
Why it matters: group vision; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R06 | anchor: A02
A disability does not automatically bar licensing: the deciding question is whether the condition keeps the person from driving safely, and a restricted license is possible when it does not. [A02]
Why it matters: group health; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R07 | anchor: A03
Regular license classes and commercial license classes share the letters A, B and C, but a regular Class C is the ordinary noncommercial license that most car and small-truck drivers need. [A03]
Why it matters: group classes; confusable regular Class C versus commercial Class C.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R08 | anchor: A03
The regular Class A threshold is about the towed unit, rated 10,001 pounds or more, while the regular Class B threshold is about a single vehicle rated 26,001 pounds or more. [A03]
Why it matters: group classes; difficulty high.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R09 | anchor: A04
A commercial Class C vehicle is defined by what it carries, sixteen or more people counting the driver or placarded hazardous materials, not by weight alone. [A04]
Why it matters: group classes; confusable with regular Class C weight limit.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R10 | anchor: A04
A motorcycle endorsement is added to an existing regular or commercial license, while a motorcycle learner permit is a separate permit; either one allows motorcycle operation on public roads. [A04]
Why it matters: group endorsements; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R11 | anchor: A04
A school bus driver needs a School Bus Driver's Certificate on top of the CDL endorsements, while a school activity bus driver meets the same requirements without that certificate. [A04]
Why it matters: group endorsements; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R12 | anchor: A03
In the three-point turnabout the wheel goes left on both forward moves and right on the backward move. [A03]
Why it matters: group skills; mnemonic Left, Right, Left.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0012]
